_meta: A set of value vectors (given as scalars for clarity) and an MLP, used to show that a self-attention layer's output is a softmax-weighted average of the value vectors -- a convex combination -- so it always lies within the convex hull of its inputs and can never produce a value outside their range, while the MLP (feedforward) applies a nonlinearity per token and can produce outputs outside that range. This is the structural reason a transformer needs both blocks and the correction to the common belief that 'attention is where the computation happens.' Attention moves information between positions: each output is sum of weight_i times value_i, with the weights a softmax (all non-negative, summing to one), so the output is a weighted average and is bounded below by the smallest value and above by the largest -- no matter what the attention weights are, attention cannot compute a value the inputs do not already bracket, and in particular cannot compute a nonlinear function of a single token's features. The MLP is where per-token nonlinear computation lives: a hidden layer with a nonlinearity (here relu) followed by a projection maps a single value to an output that can leave the input range entirely. On this fixture the values are 1, 3, 2, so every attention output lies in [1, 3] for every weighting, while the MLP maps 3 to 4 (above the range) and 1 to 0 (below it). The values, several attention weightings, and the MLP parameters are the fixture; every attention output, its bracketing, and the MLP outputs are computed. Stdlib only.
